## How a switched-off dependency is actually skipped

A capability set to 0 does two things: it defines `MT_ENABLE_<DEP>=0` for the
compiler, which compiles the calling code out, and it must stop the dependency
from being **built** at all. The second half is the expensive one -- the image
codec bundle alone is 541 MB of source and build tree -- and it works differently
on each platform.

Every dependency script gates itself on `$MT_ENABLE_<DEP>` / `$env:MT_ENABLE_<DEP>`
and, when off, writes a **stub archive** instead of building. The stub carries one
dummy symbol and no library symbols, because the engine and app projects name
these archives on the link line unconditionally -- an absent file is a link error,
not a saving. Anything that still calls into the dependency fails at link time,
which is the intended outcome: that code should have been compiled out by the
matching `MT_ENABLE_*` define.

**The gate must come before the submodule check.** With the capability off, an
app's build script never fetches the submodule -- that is the point of selective
acquisition -- so a missing-submodule error ahead of the gate turns the saving
into a build failure on any clean clone.

**Absent means ON.** A flag missing from the resolved fragment is treated as 1
(`${MT_ENABLE_FTXUI:-1}` on macOS, the same rule in `Import-MTCapsEnvironment` on
Windows), so a bare engine build with no manifest still builds everything.

**Both paths must stamp.** A script that stamps only the stub leaves that stamp
beside a real archive after the capability is switched back on; the next off build
then matches the stamp, skips, and keeps the real archive while believing it wrote
a stub.

### Where the flags come from

| platform | mechanism |
|---|---|
| macOS | Dependency builds are Xcode **script phases**. Xcode exports every build setting from the resolved `MTEngineCaps.xcconfig` into the phase environment automatically, so the scripts just read `$MT_ENABLE_*`. |
| Windows | Nothing does this for free. `build-deps.ps1` takes `-CapsFile` (the same `MTEngineCaps.xcconfig`) and calls `Import-MTCapsEnvironment`, which publishes the `MT_ENABLE_*` lines into the process environment before any library script runs. An app's build script must pass it. |

Linux publishes them the same way Windows now does, from `build-linux.sh` via
`mt_caps_read_flags`; that half was always there.

### Coverage

Every acquisition script gates itself. As of 2026-08-27:

| dependency | macOS | Linux | Windows |
|---|---|---|---|
| mbedTLS | gate | gate | gate |
| FTXUI | gate | gate | gate |
| llama.cpp | gate | n/a (not built) | gate |
| image codecs | gate | gate | gate |
| video codecs | gate | gate | gate |
| SDL2/SDL3, uSockets | core -- no capability, never gated | | |

Before that date the picture was far patchier, and it is worth recording what was
wrong because the failure was silent in every case -- a dependency that builds
when it should not produces a working binary, just a much more expensive one.

**Windows could not read the flags at all.** MSBuild properties are not
environment variables, and nothing converted the resolved fragment into either.
The one gate that existed (`build-mbedtls.ps1`) therefore could never fire, and
`build-deps.ps1` built llama.cpp, FTXUI, mbedTLS and the image codecs on every
build whatever the manifest said. `build-ftxui.ps1`, `build-llama-cpp.ps1` and
`build-image_codecs.ps1` had no gate at all.

**Linux had the plumbing but two missing gates**: `build-ftxui.sh` and
`build-image_codecs.sh`.

**Two bundles had no gate on any platform.** The image codecs -- TIFF, WebP, AVIF,
libgav1, LibRaw, libjxl, lcms2 -- which is why a C64 debugger with `MT_CAP_RAW=0`
still compiled LibRaw; and the video codecs -- FFmpeg, libvpx, opus -- built even
with `MT_CAP_VIDEO_PLAYBACK=0`.

Because that bundle is one archive serving six flags, it is skipped only when
`MT_ENABLE_LIBTIFF`, `MT_ENABLE_LIBWEBP`, `MT_ENABLE_LIBAVIF`, `MT_ENABLE_LIBHEIF`,
`MT_ENABLE_LIBRAW` and `MT_ENABLE_LCMS2` are all 0 -- any one of them still wanted
means building it, as there is no per-codec archive to stub. `libjxl` has no
capability of its own: it decodes JPEG XL DNGs, a RAW concern, so it travels with
`MT_ENABLE_LIBRAW`.

## Core dependencies

Always-on, belonging to no capability. **A `LICENSES.txt` derived from the
resolved capability set alone would omit every one of these** and ship a
legally incomplete SBOM while looking complete.

| Dependency | Licence | Version | Provenance |
|---|---|---|---|
| SDL3 | Zlib | vendored | vendored source, CMakeLists.txt:133-146 (FATAL_ERROR if absent) |
| Dear ImGui | MIT | 1.93.0 WIP | vendored source, src/Engine/Libs/imgui |
| ImPlot | MIT | vendored | vendored source; core because VID_Main.cpp:198 creates its context and ImPlotColorsExtensionGetterCallback is in the MT_API.h contract |
| zlib | Zlib | vendored | compiled straight into the engine, CMakeLists.txt:899-913 |
| ALSA | LGPL-2.1 | system | system package, find_package(ALSA REQUIRED) at CMakeLists.txt:147 (Linux) |
| GTK3 | LGPL-2.1 | system | system package, pkg_check_modules(GTK3 REQUIRED) (Linux) |
| freetype | FTL or GPL-2.0 | committed prebuilt | committed prebuilt, platform/Windows/libs |
| libuv | MIT | committed prebuilt | committed prebuilt, platform/Windows/libs |
| libicc / sRGB profile | see src/Engine/Libs/icc | vendored | core: on the render path, no third-party dependency. NOT the same thing as MT_CAP_COLOR_MANAGEMENT, which is Color/ and lcms2 |
| EXIF reader | engine source | vendored | core: Core/CImageData.cpp:21 includes CExifReader.h unconditionally, no third-party dependency |
| i18n | engine source | n/a | core by decision 4 -- c64d is due to be localised |
| audio (SND, channels, ogg/tremor) | BSD-3-Clause (Ogg/Tremor) | vendored | core: every app has it on, it is on the MT_API.h path, and a key that cannot change the build is configuration without capability |

## Commercial-mode effects

`MT_COMMERCIAL_BUILD` is **not** a whole-capability veto. Three values:
`none`, `capability-off` (the whole capability is withheld) and `variant`
(the capability stays **on** and a subset of its libraries or decoders is
withheld) — `variant` is the common case.

| Capability | Effect | Withheld in a commercial build |
|---|---|---|
| `MT_CAP_PHOTO_CODECS` | variant | heif |
| `MT_CAP_VIDEO_PLAYBACK` | variant | hevc, wmv1, wmv2, wmv3, vc1, wmav1, wmav2, aac, eac3 |

## Distribution tiers

`MT_COMMERCIAL_BUILD` alone describes two tiers, and there are **three**.
`MT_PRIVATE_BUILD` supplies the missing distinction.

| Tier | `MT_PRIVATE_BUILD` | `MT_COMMERCIAL_BUILD` | May link distribution-restricted deps |
|---|---|---|---|
| Private — built and kept, never handed to anyone | `1` | `0` | **yes** |
| Public / free — distributed at no cost, e.g. a GitHub release | `0` | `0` | no |
| Commercial — sold or app-store distributed | `0` | `1` | no |

Setting both to `1` is a configure-time error: an artifact is either sold
or never distributed, and only its author can say which.

**Open source is not the same question.** A permissive or copyleft source
licence settles *copyright*. A dependency can additionally carry *patent*
obligations that attach to **distribution itself**, whether or not money
changes hands — HEVC, reached through libheif, is the case in this tree.
So a fully public MIT project is *not* automatically eligible; the tier
above is what decides, not the repository's licence. This is also why the
gate is a separate key rather than something derived from
`MT_COMMERCIAL_BUILD`: free public distribution sits between the two.

Distribution-restricted today: `MT_ENABLE_LIBHEIF`
(`PRIVATE_ONLY_FLAGS` in `tools/mtcaps/resolve.py`). Kept per **library**,
not per capability, so the BSD-family siblings under the same
`MT_CAP_PHOTO_CODECS` key — TIFF, WebP, AVIF — are never collateral.

Separately and for an unrelated reason, `PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE_FLAGS` in the
same file forces a flag off where the library simply has not been vendored
yet — libheif on Windows today. That is an engineering gap, not a policy:
it applies in **every** tier, private included, and the entry disappears
when someone does the porting work.

## Descriptions

### `MT_CAP_CAMERA`

Live camera capture. c64d needs it for C64 Ultimate support (decision 5).

*Core/CCameraCapture.cpp:3 already guards the platform factory on MT_CAMERA_CAPTURE_ENABLED and :17-21 falls back to new CCameraDummy(). The off-path is written and compiling.*

*On Linux the define is not the whole story: CMakeLists.txt:916 compiles platform/Linux/src.Linux/CCameraLinux.cpp and :949 links v4l2, both unconditionally. Both move behind the capability. v4l2 is a SYSTEM PACKAGE, so decision H applies -- a Linux manifest asking for camera without it fails the configure naming the install command.*

### `MT_CAP_COLOR_MANAGEMENT`

Colour-management engines and DCP profile handling (Color/). NOT ICC parsing, which is core: Libs/icc is on the render path with no third-party dependency, and conflating the two is a mistake this design made twice.

*Color/CDcpApply.cpp:3 and CDcpTemperature.cpp:2 include DevelopMath.h.*

### `MT_CAP_CRASH_REPORTER`

Crash reporting (MT_CrashReporter).

*The off-path has precedent: it is already headless-aware ('CrashReporter: disabled (headless=1 ...)').*

### `MT_CAP_DEVELOP`

RAW development maths and pipeline (Develop/).

*Verified by the includes: Develop/DevelopMath.cpp:3 includes CRawDecoder.h. The WORK ORDER in #5.5 is the opposite direction -- gate RAW first, because a guard on DEVELOP written before RAW has a stub has nothing to degrade to.*

### `MT_CAP_FTXUI`

Terminal UI toolkit, linked and used directly by the app.

*LightHeroes guards on MT_ENABLE_FTXUI in six of its own sites, and in the `#if X` style -- so on Linux and Windows, where the flag is defined nowhere, its admin dashboard is OFF today and a value-style normalisation would turn it ON.*

*It keeps the library name deliberately. A dependency-only capability has no engine feature to abstract -- no engine source includes ftxui, verified zero hits in src/ -- so the app links ftxui's API directly and the library name IS the feature name. Renaming it MT_CAP_TERMINAL_UI would also collide with MT_CAP_TERMINAL, a different capability.*

### `MT_CAP_GAMEPADS`

Gamepad support: the SDL gamepad layer and Core/GamePads.

### `MT_CAP_HTTP`

Plain HTTP client (cpp-httplib) and the shared file downloader.

*MT_CAP_HTTP OWNS cpp-httplib. MT_CAP_LLM depends on it and must not own it: Tools/NetGame/CFileDownloader.cpp is a shared consumer independent of any LLM, so leaving httplib inside the llama.cpp submodule makes a plain HTTP-only app pay for a 598 MB dependency to download a file.*

### `MT_CAP_HTTPS`

TLS for the HTTP client, via mbedTLS.

*MT_ENABLE_MBEDTLS appears in Libs/httplib/httplib.h:21, a header app TUs include, and it changes httplib::Client's STRUCT LAYOUT. This is the ODR case: an engine built with it on and an app TU compiled with it off stack-allocate different-sized Clients. c64d exhibits it on macOS and Windows today.*

### `MT_CAP_KTX2`

KTX2 / basis_universal texture transcoding.

*Core/CKTX2Loader.cpp has NO preprocessor guard today and is consumed unconditionally by CImageData.cpp, so unlike every other capability here there is no existing off-path to switch on. It needs the CImageDataTIFF.cpp treatment -- guard the body, keep the header unconditional, keep the file in all three build lists, #else-stub the entry points -- before it can be gated at all.*

### `MT_CAP_LLM`

Local large-language-model inference via llama.cpp, plus model discovery and download.

*HTTPS, not merely HTTP, and it is settled rather than assumed: CLlamaModelManager.cpp:228 builds EVERY model URL as https://huggingface.co/..., and httplib::Client on an https:// host without TLS support fails at runtime. LLM=1 HTTPS=0 would build, link and be unable to fetch any model -- the succeeds-and-lies shape #3.4 abolishes. There is no plain-HTTP model source in the tree, so splitting the downloader would buy a configuration nothing uses.*

*No app guards on MT_ENABLE_LLAMA_CPP. Measured by grepping all four app src/ trees.*

### `MT_CAP_MIDI`

MIDI input and output via rtmidi.

### `MT_CAP_MUSIC_PLAYER`

Music player and playlists. LightHeroes only.

*It does NOT imply an AUDIO capability: audio is CORE and has no vocabulary key, so an implication onto it would make mtcaps exit 2 on an unknown key. The coupling is real and is stated here as prose: the music player needs the core audio path, which is always present.*

### `MT_CAP_NET_GAME`

Networked-game session layer (Tools/NetGame).

*Gating NET_GAME without these gates nothing, and its acceptance criterion then passes vacuously.*

### `MT_CAP_NET_TRANSPORT`

Reliable UDP transport (ENet) and Core/Net.

### `MT_CAP_PHOTO_CODECS`

Still-image codecs beyond the core set: TIFF, WebP, AVIF and HEIF.

*PhotoCruise guards on MT_ENABLE_LIBTIFF, MT_ENABLE_LIBWEBP (x2), MT_ENABLE_LIBAVIF and MT_ENABLE_LIBHEIF in its own src/Tests/CTestFormatSupport.cpp. Decision E was reversed on this measurement.*

### `MT_CAP_RAW`

Camera RAW decoding via LibRaw.

*Measured: MT_ENABLE_LIBRAW appears in the four app trees only inside a COMMENT (PhotoCruise/src/PhotoCruiseInit.cpp:352) saying the opposite. It joins the app-visible set if and when a grep finds a real guard.*

### `MT_CAP_TERMINAL`

Embedded terminal emulator: libtmt and GUI/Controls/CGuiViewTerminal. A different capability from MT_CAP_FTXUI.

### `MT_CAP_TEST_ENGINE`

imgui_test_engine UI-automation harness.

*Appears in three headers app TUs include, and all four apps' src/Tests/ guard on it. Renamed from ENABLE_IMGUI_TEST_ENGINE in Phase 1 -- do not emit both spellings.*

### `MT_CAP_UNDO`

Undo/redo framework (Tools/Undo). LightHeroes only.

*No third-party dependency, so this is a CODE-SIZE capability rather than an acquisition one -- which makes it the cheapest place to prove the guard machinery without any acquisition change.*

### `MT_CAP_VIDEO_PLAYBACK`

Video decoding and playback: FFmpeg, libvpx, opus, nestegg, and the platform hardware decoders.

*MT_ENABLE_FFMPEG appears in Video/CVideoSourceFFmpeg.h:10, a header app TUs include, AND PhotoCruise guards on it 40 times in its own src/. Both routes to app-visible are exercised by this one flag.*

### `MT_CAP_WEBSOCKETS`

WebSocket server/client via uWebSockets on uSockets.

*Gated in Phase 4, not Phase 3: the uSockets consolidation in #5.4b rewrites the same archive this capability gates, so gating it first would gate a copy that is about to move.*
